topicTitle: Federalism, Centre – State Relations & Inter State Relations

prelimsCapsule.coreConceptSummary: Centrally Sponsored Schemes (CSS) are special funding mechanisms implemented by state governments or central agencies under central ministries, funded jointly by the Centre and States under Article 282 of the Constitution, forming a critical pillar of cooperative and fiscal federalism in India.
highYieldFacts: Fact 1: Funding patterns for CSS generally range from 60:40 or 90:10 for North-Eastern/Himalayan states based on historical modifications recommended by the Sub-Group of Chief Ministers on Rationalisation of CSS (2015).

Fact 2: Article 282 of the Indian Constitution serves as the financial conduit for CSS, permitting the Union or a State to make grants for any public purpose, notwithstanding that the matter is not within the legislative competence of Parliament or the State Legislature.
Fact 3: The 2016 restructuring rationalized over 150+ schemes into 28 Umbrella schemes, subsequently categorized into Core Schemes (core of core and core) and Optional Schemes.

Fact 4: The Public Financial Management System (PFMS) and the Single Nodal Agency (SNA) model introduced in 2021 mandate just-in-time fund releases, curbing diversion and enhancing fiscal transparency.
Fact 5: The 15th Finance Commission under N.K. Singh recommended performance-based conditional transfers under CSS to incentivize states on governance and human capital indicators.
trapsAndElimination: Trap 1: Assuming CSS are funded exclusively out of the Consolidated Fund of India as statutory divisible tax proceeds under Article 270. They are funded through non-tax revenues and grants-in-aid under Article 282, which are discretionary grants.
Trap 2: Confusing Central Sector Schemes (100% funded and executed by the Central Government) with Centrally Sponsored Schemes (cost-sharing between Centre and States).

mainsFramework.inDepthTheoryHtml:
Evolution and Architecture of Centrally Sponsored Schemes

Centrally Sponsored Schemes (CSS) represent the fiscal machinery through which the Union government influences socio-economic policy domains residing squarely within the State List (Schedule VII, List II) such as health, education, agriculture, and rural development. Originating in the era of centralized planning via the erstwhile Planning Commission, CSS emerged as a mechanism to bridge regional developmental deficits and push uniform national standards across disparate states. However, this architectural design historically triggered friction in India's quasi-federal framework, often criticized as an intrusion into state autonomy through conditional, top-down funding mechanisms.

Structural Reforms and Rationalization

Recognizing the friction of proliferation—where over 400 micro-schemes existed—the Government of India acted on the recommendations of the Sub-Group of Chief Ministers on Rationalisation of CSS (convened via NITI Aayog). The architecture was streamlined into Core of the Core Schemes (like MGNREGA), Core Schemes (National Health Mission, Samagra Shiksha), and Optional Schemes. Concurrently, the sharing pattern was reconfigured to 60:40 for general states and 90:10 for Himalayan and North-Eastern states. Despite these adjustments, issues persist regarding state fiscal space contraction, rigidity in local tailoring, and 'one-size-fits-all' mandates.

Contemporary Fiscal Governance and Digital Interventions

The introduction of the Single Nodal Agency (SNA) model and mandatory routing through the Public Financial Management System (PFMS) has altered fund management. States are now required to open a single escrow-type account per scheme, restricting the float time of funds and compelling states to transfer central shares along with their matching state shares within strict timelines. While this plugs leakage and optimizes public expenditure tracking, critics argue that aggressive conditionalities and delayed matching contributions from financially stressed states stall grassroots implementation.

dimensions.constitutional_or_legal: Tension between federal autonomy (State List subjects) and Union spending power under Article 282; overuse of conditional grants bypassing statutory Finance Commission devolution.
dimensions.socio_economic: Impact on human capital formation, equity across low-income states (LSI), and targeted upliftment of vulnerable demographics through welfare delivery.
dimensions.administrative_governance: Implementation hurdles, matching share burdens on cash-strapped states, bureaucratic delays, SNA-PFMS friction, and rigid vertical oversight.
dimensions.international_or_comparative: Alignment with Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs); comparative analysis with conditional grant frameworks in Australian and Canadian federalisms.

Loans received from foreign governments 3. Loans and advances granted to the States and Union Territories 4. Defence expenditure Select the correct answer using the code given below.
prelims.explanation: Defence expenditure is part of revenue expenditure (except capital outlay for defense equipment which is capital, but general defense maintenance/salaries are revenue), whereas asset creation, foreign loans, and loans to states constitute capital budget items.

modelMainsQA.question: Discuss the structural challenges associated with Centrally Sponsored Schemes (CSS) in India. How do recent financial management frameworks like the Single Nodal Agency (SNA) system impact cooperative federalism? (250 Words, 15 Marks)

approach.intro: Define Centrally Sponsored Schemes and their constitutional footing under Article 282, emphasizing their role in addressing national priorities across State List subjects.
approach.body: Detail the core structural challenges (matching share burden, rigidity, one-size-fits-all). Evaluate the SNA and PFMS framework, balancing transparency/efficiency gains against fiscal centralization and state autonomy concerns. Use committee references.
approach.conclusion: Suggest a path forward focusing on flexible conditionalities, outcome-based devolution, and genuine fiscal collaboration inline with cooperative federalism.

modelMainsQA.modelAnswerHtml:
Centrally Sponsored Schemes (CSS) constitute a major instrument for the Union government to finance socio-economic development across subjects in the State List, utilizing discretionary grants-in-aid under Article 282 of the Constitution. While instrumental in achieving national targets, they frequently spark friction within India's quasi-federal structure.

Structural Challenges in CSS:

  • Burden of Matching Shares: Financially stressed states struggle to mobilize their mandatory matching shares (e.g., 40% in general schemes), leading to stalled projects and unutilized central allocations.
  • Rigidity and 'One-Size-Fits-All' Design: Centralized design limits local customization. Schemes devised in New Delhi fail to account for topography-specific or socio-cultural diversities in southern, eastern, or northeastern states.
  • Administrative Over-centralization: Proliferation of micro-management, strict vertical conditionalities, and parallel implementation structures often bypass local self-government institutions (Panchayats and Urban Local Bodies).

Impact of the Single Nodal Agency (SNA) and PFMS Framework:

  • Efficiency & Transparency: The SNA model ensures that funds do not lie idle in multiple commercial bank accounts, tracking expenditures down to the last implementation tier through the Public Financial Management System (PFMS).
  • Fiscal Centralization vs. Cooperative Federalism: While the SNA model checks the unauthorized retention of interest earned on central funds by states, it simultaneously enhances central micro-surveillance, reducing the fiscal maneuvering space of state treasuries.

Way Forward:
As recommended by the Punchhi Commission and the NITI Aayog sub-groups, CSS must be consolidated further, with states given greater flexibility in sub-allocating funds. Transitioning from input-based conditionalities to output and outcome-based incentives will align fiscal accountability with the true spirit of cooperative and competitive federalism.

practiceMCQs.question: Consider the following statements regarding Centrally Sponsored Schemes (CSS) in India: 1. They are primarily funded through statutory grants under Article 270 of the Constitution. 2. The Single Nodal Agency (SNA) model requires state governments to open a single nodal account for every scheme to curb fund float and misuse. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceMCQs.explanation: Statement 1 is incorrect because CSS are funded through non-tax revenues and discretionary grants-in-aid under Article 282, not statutory divisible tax proceeds under Article 270. Statement 2 is correct; the SNA model mandates a single bank account per scheme to ensure 'just-in-time' fund releases and transparent tracking via PFMS.

practiceMCQs.question: Which of the following constitutional provisions is most frequently invoked by the Union Government to finance Centrally Sponsored Schemes that fall within the legislative domain of State Legislatures?
practiceMCQs.explanation: Article 282 empowers the Union or a State to make grants for any public purpose, even if the subject matter falls outside its respective legislative competence. This provision serves as the primary constitutional anchor for Centrally Sponsored Schemes.
